verses.1: And it happened that, on a Sabbath day, he went to the house of some of the leaders of the Pharisees to eat bread. They were also there to watch him.
verses.2: And I saw that there was a man who was naked in front of him.
verses.3: And when Jesus spoke, he said to the rabbis and Pharisees, “Is it proper to heal on the Sabbath?”
verses.4: But those who remained calm. And after taking his money, he dismissed him and left.
verses.5: And he said to them, “Which of your sons or oxen will fall into the pit? And will they not be rescued from it on the day of Sabbath?”
verses.6: And they were unable to respond to these things.
verses.7: He spoke to those who were called upon as a joke, explaining how the firstborn were chosen. He said to them:
verses.8: When you are called to get married by someone, do not refuse the first invitation. Even if it seems more advantageous for you to be invited by that person instead.
verses.9: And when you came to him and called out to him, he scolded you. For this reason, at that time, he began to hold the second place after being scolded.
verses.10: But when you are called to go to that upper place, so that when the one who calls you comes, he may greet you there. Friend, climb up higher. Then you will be honored in front of all those who are with you.
verses.11: For every person who elevates himself, someone else will be humbled; and for those who humble themselves, someone else will be elevated.
verses.12: He also said to him: “When you prepare a fine meal, do not speak to your friends, brothers, relatives, or wealthy neighbors. Even if they try to compensate you, it will only lead to your downfall.”
verses.13: But when you are willing to do so, then call upon the poor, the needy, the crippled, the blind.
verses.14: And it will be better if they do not have any countermeasures against you. For in the reallocation of justice, they will be dealt with accordingly.
verses.15: And someone among those present said to him, “It would be good if one could eat bread in the kingdom of God.”
verses.16: But he said to him, “Some man has prepared a great meal. He has called many people over.”
verses.17: And he sent his slave to say to those who were called to come forward: “Come, for everything is ready.”
verses.18: And they all began to resign from their positions. The first one said to him, “I have taken Agron as my wife, and I need to go and see him. I hope you will allow me to go with you.”
verses.19: And another said, “I have already used five of them for testing purposes. I’ll continue to use them in further tests. I hope you’ll accept them with me.”
verses.20: And another said, “Woman’s clothes… and because of that, I can’t go.”
verses.21: And when the slave reported these things to his master, the master became angry and said to him, “Quickly go to the streets of the city! Bring there those who are poor, those who are weak, those who are blind, and those who are crippled.”
verses.22: And the slave said, “Lord, it has happened as you commanded. And the place is still there.”
verses.23: And the Lord said to the servant, “Go into the fields and fields, and force people to come in, so that my house may be filled.”
verses.24: I tell you that none of those men who were called to eat with me had any flavor in their food.
verses.25: Many people also gathered around him. One of them said to them, “
verses.26: If someone comes to me and does not hate his father, his mother, his wife, his children, his brothers, or his sisters, and also does not hate his own soul, then such a person cannot be my disciple.
verses.27: Whoever does not tremble at the sight of the cross and comes back to me cannot be my disciple.
verses.28: After all, who among you wants to build a tower? First, one must sit down and decide whether it’s worth the cost or not.
verses.29: So that, once he is destroyed and no longer has any power, all those who observe him will begin to deceive him.
verses.30: They said that this man began to build a house, but he refused to continue with the construction.
verses.31: Or, what kind of king would go to war against another king without first seeking advice? Is it possible for him to defeat those who come with twenty thousand men, when he himself has only ten thousand men at his disposal?
verses.32: But if not, then send a representative to him, so that he can negotiate for peace.
verses.33: Thus, none of you who do not give up everything that belongs to oneself cannot be my student.
verses.34: So, the ice is good. But if even the ice melts, then where will it be used?
verses.35: It’s neither fit to be placed on the ground nor in any other place. They put it outside. Those who have ears, should listen carefully.
